about: The AP Chemistry app pages. scripts/build-apchem.mjs writes each page's shell (head, header, footer, a <div id="app"> mount) from this file; the page's behavior is its script in chem/assets/<script>, which mounts into #app. Until that script exists the shell says the page arrives with the first published unit. "static": true marks a generated page that is not an app (teachers.html). premium names the Premium feature (ApChemCore gates it); card is the line on the course home. No path may contain the token "ap" (docs/apchem-spec.md decision 2). tools[] are the trainers, skills tools and drills: page chem/tools/<slug>.html, script chem/assets/tools/<slug>.js, content chem/data/tools/<slug>.json (docs/apchem-architecture.md, Tools). None is built yet.

apps.title: Practice questions
apps.desc: Chemistry practice by unit, topic or skill: stimulus sets and calculations graded on value, units and significant figures, with every option explained.
apps.card: Drill a unit, a topic or a science practice, with stimulus sets.

apps.title: Spaced review
apps.desc: Your chemistry spaced review queue: every question you missed comes back just before you would forget it.
apps.card: Missed questions come back when you are about to forget them.

apps.title: Unit tests and practice exams
apps.desc: Timed chemistry unit tests and full practice exams in the real format: 60 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes, then 7 free-response questions.
apps.card: Unit tests and full timed practice exams in the real 60 + 7 format.

apps.title: Free-response practice
apps.desc: Chemistry free-response practice, long and short questions, each with a point-by-point rubric, a full-credit sample answer and a printable answer sheet.
apps.card: Long and short free-response questions, with rubrics and sample answers.

apps.title: Justification trainer
apps.desc: Chemistry explain and justify practice: write an answer, check it against a rubric, and compare an answer that earns the point with one that does not.
apps.lede: Free-response points are lost on vague reasons. Write your answer, check it against the rubric, then see one answer that earns the point and one that sounds right but does not, and why.
apps.card: Explain and justify prompts with a rubric checklist and two model answers.

apps.title: Cram kit
apps.desc: Chemistry cram plans counted back from your exam date: three or two weeks, day by day, weighted by unit, with unit sheets, timed mixed sets and practice exams.
apps.lede: A 3-week or 2-week plan counted back from your exam date, day by day: unit sheets and notes, a timed mixed set and one free-response question each study day, two full practice exams and rest days. Print it and tick the days off.
apps.card: 3-week and 2-week plans to exam day, and timed mixed sets.

apps.title: Flashcards
apps.desc: Spaced-repetition chemistry flashcards built from the glossary, by unit and topic.

apps.title: Trainers and drills
apps.desc: Chemistry trainers and drills: justifications, particle diagrams, equilibrium and buffer drills, titration curves, each followed by questions.
apps.card: Trainers and drills, then the questions about what you did.

apps.title: Your dashboard
apps.desc: Your chemistry mastery by unit, topic and science practice, with every miss linked to the lesson that teaches it.
apps.card: Mastery by unit, topic and science practice.

apps.title: Search the course
apps.desc: Search every chemistry lesson, notes page, glossary term and tool in the course.

apps.title: For teachers
apps.desc: For chemistry teachers: stable share links, printable notes and unit sheets, and sharing pages to Google Classroom, with no new student data collected.
apps.lede: Share any notes page, lesson or unit sheet with a stable link. Students need no account, and nothing they do leaves their device unless they choose to sign in.
